c.tagline: A pastel-walled colonial port on the Gulf, ramparts and bastions guarding a UNESCO old town.

taxi.fareNote: Campeche's street taxis are mostly unmetered, so agree the fare before setting off (short trips around the walled centre are cheap); Uber and DiDi operate with limited driver numbers but give an upfront price.

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's unified emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 078 is the national tourist assistance line.

hood_landmark.Centro Histórico (Ciudad Amurallada): the walled old town's Puerta de Tierra gate and pastel streets
hood_landmark.San Román: Iglesia de San Román, home of the revered Cristo Negro
hood_landmark.Barrio de Santa Ana: the Iglesia de Santa Ana and its traditional cocina económica eateries
hood_landmark.Guadalupe: Iglesia de Guadalupe, one of the peninsula's oldest churches
hood_landmark.San Francisco: Iglesia de San Francisco, among the earliest churches on the American mainland

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed walled old town of pastel colonial houses, cobbled streets, bastions (baluartes) and the land-and-sea gates; best for first-timers who want every sight, restaurant and the seafront Malecón within an easy walk.

A characterful barrio just outside the walls, predating the fortifications, centred on the church of San Román and its revered Black Christ; more lived-in and local than the restored centre, with good-value guesthouses.

One of the oldest colourful barrios abutting the northern walls, with a lively little plaza, the Santa Ana gate and pockets of nightlife and street food; suits travelers who want atmosphere a few steps from the centre.
A convenient residential barrio just south of the walls near the ADO bus station and shops, an easy walk to the historic core; practical and quieter, with mid-range hotels and everyday local life.

A historic district north of the centre where Hernández de Córdoba first landed, with colonial churches, street art and the hilltop fort of San José el Alto above; calmer and residential, a short ride from the walls.
lodging: Hacienda Puerta Campeche, a Luxury Collection Hotel

water.note: Stick to bottled or purified water, as everywhere in Mexico.

transit.pay: Bus and colectivo fares are paid in cash to the driver (roughly MXN 8-12); there is no rechargeable transit card. Keep small change handy.
transit.hours: City buses and colectivos run roughly 5:30 AM to around 10:00 PM; taxis and ride apps fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Campeche has no metro or rail transit; the compact walled Centro is best explored on foot, with city buses, colectivo combis and taxis covering the barrios and the Malecón. The panoramic 'Guagua' tram-bus runs tourist loops from the Plaza Principal.

air: Ingeniero Alberto Acuña Ongay International Airport (CPE)

airport.name: Ingeniero Alberto Acuña Ongay International Airport (CPE)

transit.m: Authorized airport taxi to the Centro Histórico, ~15 min

tip.r: Around 10-15% at restaurants is customary; rounding up for taxis and leaving small change for hotel and bar staff is appreciated.
